content: 1. The Inter-agency Field Manual on Reproductive Health in Humanitarian Settings provides comprehensive guidance on addressing reproductive health needs in crisis situations. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 2. The Consolidated Guidelines on the Use of Antiretroviral Drugs for Treating and Preventing HIV Infection outlines public health recommendations for managing HIV. This second edition was accessed on August 25, 2021. 3. Research by Zachariah et al. (2002) highlights that moderate to severe malnutrition in tuberculosis (TB) patients significantly increases the risk of early mortality. This study was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 4. The Guideline: Updates on the Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition in Infants and Children provides updated strategies for addressing malnutrition in vulnerable populations. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 5. The WHO Child Growth Standards and the Identification of Severe Acute Malnutrition in Infants and Children is a joint statement by WHO and UNICEF, offering criteria for identifying malnutrition. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 6. Davies et al. (2006) explored the epidemiological link between smoking and tuberculosis, as well as the immunopathogenesis of this association. This study was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 7. The Diagnosis and Management of Type 2 Diabetes (HEARTS-D) document provides clinical guidance for managing diabetes. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 8. The mhGAP Humanitarian Intervention Guide (mhGAP-HIG) offers clinical management strategies for mental, neurological, and substance use conditions in humanitarian emergencies. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 9. Alene et al. (2018) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of mental health disorders, social stressors, and health-related quality of life in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. This study was published in the Journal of Infection. 10. Lönnroth et al. (2008) systematically reviewed the role of alcohol use as a risk factor for tuberculosis. This study was published in BMC Public Health. 11. Getahun et al. (2013) discussed strategies for managing tuberculosis in individuals who use or inject illicit drugs. This was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 12. The Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) manual provides tools for primary care providers to screen for substance use. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 13. The Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Prevention, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Care for Key Populations (2016 update) offers comprehensive recommendations for managing HIV in vulnerable groups. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 14. WHO's Integrating Collaborative TB and HIV Services within a Comprehensive Package of Care for People Who Inject Drugs provides guidelines for addressing co-infections. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 15. Bissell et al. (2021) emphasized the importance of smoking cessation and smoke-free environments for tuberculosis patients in the second edition of their guidelines. 16. The Prioritizing Diseases for Research and Development in Emergency Contexts document outlines strategies for addressing health challenges in crises. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 17. Qiu et al. (2021) analyzed the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on health, culture, and society, emphasizing its effects on tuberculosis detection and mortality. 18. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 19. The Preparedness, Prevention, and Control of Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) for Refugees and Migrants in Non-Camp Settings offers interim guidance for managing outbreaks in vulnerable populations. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 20. The End TB Strategy outlines global targets and strategies for tuberculosis prevention, care, and control post-2015. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 21. WHO's Operational Handbook on Tuberculosis provides detailed modules on screening, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of tuberculosis, including drug-resistant forms. These modules were accessed on August 25, 2021. 22. The BCG Vaccines: WHO Position Paper (February 2018) discusses the role of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccines in tuberculosis prevention. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 23. WHO's Guidelines for the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis and Patient Care (2017 update) provides evidence-based recommendations for managing TB. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 24. The Global Laboratory Initiative offers a practical guide to strengthening tuberculosis laboratory services. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 25. WHO's Ethics Guidance for the Implementation of the End TB Strategy emphasizes ethical considerations in tuberculosis care and prevention. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 26. The Toolkit to Develop a National Strategic Plan for TB Prevention, Care, and Control provides a methodology for creating effective national strategies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 27. WHO's Guidance for National Tuberculosis Programmes on the Management of Tuberculosis in Children (second edition) offers pediatric-specific recommendations. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 28. The Framework for Conducting Reviews of Tuberculosis Programmes provides tools for evaluating and improving TB program performance. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 29. WHO's Guideline: Nutritional Care and Support for Patients with Tuberculosis highlights the importance of addressing malnutrition in TB management. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 30. The WHO Policy on Collaborative TB/HIV Activities provides guidelines for integrating tuberculosis and HIV services. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 31. WHO's Electronic Recording and Reporting for Tuberculosis Care and Control emphasizes the importance of digital tools in TB management. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 32. The Tuberculosis Laboratory Biosafety Manual (2012) outlines safety protocols for TB laboratories. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 33. WHO's ENGAGE-TB Approach provides operational guidance for integrating community-based TB activities. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 34. The WHO/Union Monograph on TB and Tobacco Control highlights the intersection of tuberculosis and tobacco use, advocating for joint control efforts. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 35. WHO's Policy on TB Infection Control in Health-Care Facilities, Congregate Settings, and Households provides infection prevention strategies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 36. The Tuberculosis and Air Travel: Guidelines for Prevention and Control (third edition) addresses TB transmission risks during air travel. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 37. WHO's Emergency Response Framework provides a structured approach to managing public health emergencies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 38. The Sphere Handbook: Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Response (fourth edition) outlines best practices for humanitarian interventions. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 39. WHO's Guidance for Contingency Planning offers tools for preparing for and responding to emergencies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 40.
